title: Halve eight tomatoes in one pass
instruction: Halve all eight cherry tomatoes in one pass. Leave all sixteen halves in the tray and both tools on their rests.
context: Cherry tomatoes are often halved for salads. A shallow tray and a loose lid let a cook steady several rolling tomatoes together and portion a batch with one knife pass.
setup: Eight 28 mm cherry tomatoes (12 g each) lie in one layer in a 170 × 154 mm rigid plastic tray with a 10 mm rim. A washable locating insert has four 8 mm-high ribs around each fruit to limit rolling under load. Its floor is 80 mm above the worktop. A loose clear plastic lid (160 × 144 × 6 mm) with a green grip rests on the left. An unpowered kitchen knife with a 177 × 22 × 1.4 mm steel blade and a 92 × 20 × 18 mm plastic handle lies in front of the tray, with the handle on two rests on the right. The worktop, tray platform and three tool supports are fixed. The two parallel grippers start open. The README and fruit.json give the fixed layout.
scoring: Score the largest batch cut in a single pass. Count C distinct tomatoes cut in that pass and H of their halves wholly in the tray and resting at the end. If passes tie on C, use the one with more retained halves. Award 0.0875 × C + 0.0125 × H. Add 0.10 for eight in one pass with all sixteen halves retained and both tools returned, released and stationary. Eight individual cuts earn at most 0.1125. Two batches of four earn at most 0.45. A single complete batch earns up to 1.0. The README defines the tolerances.
reset_notes: Use eight fresh, uniformly red, intact tomatoes from one lot, 27–29 mm across and at 20–22 °C. Rinse, blot dry and place one stem-scar up in each seat. Fit washable pad covers and a spill tray. Check blade clearance with an inert replica. Between trials, clean and dry the equipment, inspect the pads and ribs, and stop if juice enters a joint. See the README for the full procedure.
fidelity: A passive contact proxy applies equal and opposite cutting loads to the tool and each intact fruit. A draw across a centered chord under the lid and work against resistance qualify a split into two independently moving halves. The README gives the force reference, assumptions and limits. Crushing, juice and post-split blade drag are omitted.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.000 (750 actions). Scripted demonstration: 1.000 (466 actions), reproduced in an independent run with seed 0.
